The vulnerability is rooted in kernel streaming components and requires local execution to trigger, making the attack vector clear and well-defined.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker exploits CVE-2024-35250, a local untrusted pointer dereference vulnerability in the Microsoft Windows Kernel-Mode Driver (MSKSSRV), to escalate privileges by using IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY with KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET flag and manipulating KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream properties. The attack leverages kernel streaming components including ksthunk.sys and ks.sys, utilizing KsSynchronousIoControlDevice for privilege escalation.

indicators.context: Microsoft Windows Kernel-Mode Driver contains an untrusted pointer dereference vulnerability that allows a local attacker to escalate privileges

Taiwanese cybersecurity company DEVCORE, which discovered and reported CVE-2024-35250, shared additional technical details in August 2024, stating it's rooted in the Microsoft Kernel Streaming Service (MSKSSRV)

In the IOCtl_KS_PROPERTY of Kernel Streaming, to increase efficiency, KSPROPERTY_TYPE_SERIALIZESET and KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET requests are provided to allow users to operate on multiple properties through a single call

If we give the property set as KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream, there is additional processing at [5]. At [6], we can see that it first checks whether Irp->RequestorMode is KernelMode(0). If it is called from user, it will directly return an error
ks!UnserializePropertySet uses KsSynchronousIoControlDevice to perform the IOCTL again. At this point, the new Irp->RequestorMode will become KernelMode(0)

In the IOCtl_KS_PROPERTY of Kernel Streaming, to increase efficiency, KSPROPERTY_TYPE_SERIALIZESET and KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET requests are provided to allow users to operate on multiple properties through a single call

The function where IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest is used in Kernel Streaming is in ks!KsSynchronousIoControlDevice and it obviously involves calling IOCTL in the kernel using the aforementioned method. However, it appears that Irp->RequestorMode is properly set here, and different values are assigned based on the parameters of KsSynchronousIoControlDevice. This will be a convenient library for kernel streaming driver developers

ks.sys is one of the core components of Kernel Streaming. It is the library of Kernel Streaming responsible for forwarding requests such as IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY to the corresponding device driver, and it also handles functions related to AVStream
portcls.sys CVE-2024-38055 (out-of-bounds read when set dataformat for Pin) CVE-2024-38056
ks!UnserializePropertySet will handle your request. Let's take a look at UnserializePropertySet

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker sends phishing emails containing hyperlinks to download NetWire RAT malware. The malware uses anti-analysis techniques like dynamic code extraction and anti-sandboxing, then establishes persistence via registry keys, relocates itself to AppData folders, collects system information including credentials, and communicates with a C2 server using DNS resolution.

indicators.context: The downloaded file is a 7z file, which contains the new variant of NetWire RAT. After decompressing it, we are able to get an EXE file with the name of "PROFORMA-INVOICE 0990.exe".
The downloaded file is a 7z file, which contains the new variant of NetWire RAT.
Its domain is found in the decrypted string, which for this variant is "gbam0001.duckdns[.]org:3366".

It checks to see if the current executable file is located in the correct folder (%AppData%\Install) and has the right file name (Host.exe). If not, it relocates the file into "%AppData%\Install" and renames it as "Host.exe".
NetWire continues to create its home key (HKCU\SOFTWARE\NetWire) as well as adding it into the auto-run group in the victim's registry.
NetWire creates a log folder to store the log files of information that it collects from the victim's system. The log folder is located at "%AppData%\Logs".

It then calls the _beginthreadex() function to start a thread, the thread function of which registers a window class, whose window procedure function is a keylogger.

The second attack used Bookcode malware in a supply chain attack through a South Korean software company, leveraging compromised web servers as C2 infrastructure.

pipeline.attack_summary: The Epic Turla campaign uses spearphishing emails with malicious PDF or SCR attachments to exploit vulnerabilities like CVE-2013-3346 (Adobe Reader) and CVE-2013-5065 (Windows XP/2003), leading to privilege escalation. Attackers also use watering hole techniques targeting websites with outdated CMS platforms like TYPO3, injecting JavaScript and PHP scripts to exploit Java and Flash vulnerabilities. Once compromised, victims are infected with the Epic backdoor (Tavdig/Wipbot) which communicates via HTTP C&C channels, later upgraded to more sophisticated Carbon/Cobra systems for advanced persistence and lateral movement.

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Phishing .url File Triggering iediagcmd.exe with WebDAV Path
id: 41a6b8d4-7f9c-4e0a-a9d4-7a2b8d1c3e5f
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects the initial access phase of an attack where a user opens a malicious .url file from a phishing email. The .url file exploits CVE-2025-33053 to manipulate the working directory of iediagcmd.exe, causing it to execute route.exe from an attacker-controlled WebDAV server path.
references:
    - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2025-33053
    - https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/stealth-falcon-zero-day/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\iediagcmd.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\\summerartcamp[.]net@ssl@443\\DavWWWRoot\\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of iediagcmd.exe with WebDAV paths (rare)
level: high

title: Execution of route.exe Loader from Attacker-Controlled WebDAV Server
id: 7ecae33f-e2ee-46e3-a185-a06e5eefa7bf
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule identifies the execution of route.exe, a malicious loader that is downloaded and executed from an attacker-controlled WebDAV server. The loader is used to inject shellcode into Edge browser processes as part of the multi-stage attack.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17

    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\route.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\\summerartcamp[.]net@ssl@443\\DavWWWRoot\\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of route.exe for network diagnostics (uncommon)
level: high

title: Command and Control Communication via C2 Domains with RC4 Decoded Parameters
id: 34cf65db-3bff-4685-bf83-c9d91e0019a8
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects command and control (C2) communication using C2 domains with RC4-decoded query parameters. The technique involves encoding C2 endpoints to evade detection.
references:
    - https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/stealth-falcon-zero-day/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071.004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
    - attack.t1071.004
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'jNNsw'
            - 'PjH1BHszPooXyiHS3s'
            - 'uukEQ38A'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of cmd.exe with RC4-decoded parameters (rare)
level: high

title: Credential Access via Injection into UserAccessBroker.exe
id: f3b76e1c-86ab-4d4e-9293-df7203488e31
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule identifies the injection of code into UserAccessBroker.exe, a Windows system process, to extract credentials. The technique involves memory manipulation and is part of the credential access phase.
references:
    - https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/stealth-falcon-zero-day/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.credential-access

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\UserAccessBroker.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'WriteProcessMemory'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of UserAccessBroker.exe with memory manipulation (rare)
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: Attack begins with a spearphishing email containing a .url file that exploits CVE-2025-33053 to manipulate the working directory of iediagcmd.exe, causing it to execute malicious route.exe from an attacker-controlled WebDAV server. The route.exe loader uses code obfuscation and memory manipulation techniques to inject shellcode into Edge browser processes, ultimately delivering a custom Mythic-based implant named Horus Agent. The attack chain includes use of LOLBins like DeviceCredentialDeployment.exe, multiple C2 domains, and various anti-analysis measures including API hashing and string encryption.

attack_vector.reasoning: The article explicitly describes the vulnerability as an authentication bypass in ScreenConnect that allows adversaries to create privileged accounts for remote control. The attack is clearly described as initial access via exploitation of a public-facing application, with no mention of researcher workflow or patch analysis.

pipeline.attack_summary: Threat actors exploited CVE-2024-1709/CVE-2024-1708 in ScreenConnect to gain initial access, then deployed ransomware (LockBit, others), cryptocurrency miners, and additional remote access tools like Simple Help RMM and Google Chrome Remote Desktop. They used PowerShell, curl, certutil for downloads, cleared logs with wevtutil.exe, and established persistence via scheduled tasks, WMI event consumers, and registry modifications.

The malware steals credentials from browsers and Signal, and can send messages as the victim.

title: Commvault Pre-Auth Command Injection via Argument Injection in Login Endpoint
id: 5e7c8a2b-9d4f-4e6a-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a7b8
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of a pre-authentication command injection vulnerability in Commvault's authentication endpoint by injecting arguments into the commserver parameter to bypass hostname checks and execute malicious commands.
references:
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/guess-who-would-be-stupid-enough-to-rob-the-same-vault-twice-pre-auth-rce-chains-in-commvault/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1056/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1606/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1078.004
    - attack.t1566.002
    - attack.t1056.003
    - attack.t1606.001
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_path:
        cs-uri-stem: /commandcenter/api/Login
    selection_body:
        request_body|contains:
            - '"commserver":".*-cs .*"'
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using similar argument patterns in commserver fields
level: critical

title: Execution of qlogin Command with Injected Arguments for Privilege Escalation
id: 6f8d9b3c-0e5a-1f6b-2c7d-3e8f4a9b0c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of qlogin command with injected arguments through DoQlogin method, which is part of the attack chain to escalate privileges and bypass authentication in Commvault.
references:
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/guess-who-would-be-stupid-enough-to-rob-the-same-vault-twice-pre-auth-rce-chains-in-commvault/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1078.002
    - attack.t1548.004
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_cmdline:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'qlogin -cs '
            - '-csn '
            - '-gt -u '
            - '-clp '
    condition: selection_cmdline
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts invoking qlogin with valid arguments
level: high

title: Execution of QCommand to Drop JSP Webshell in Commvault Webroot
id: 7a9b8c7d-6e5f-4d3c-2b1a-0f9e8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of QCommands that drop a JSP webshell into the Commvault webroot directory, enabling persistent access and remote code execution after successful authentication bypass.
references:
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/guess-who-would-be-stupid-enough-to-rob-the-same-vault-twice-pre-auth-rce-chains-in-commvault/

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up explicitly describes exploitation of CVE-2023-27532 through unauthenticated access over port 9401, followed by SQL shell command execution that triggers PowerShell script loading. The attack chain is clearly outlined with specific telemetry indicators.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker exploited CVE-2023-27532 in Veeam Backup & Replication to gain unauthenticated access via TCP port 9401, executing PowerShell scripts including POWERTRASH for initial compromise. The attack involved credential theft, discovery commands, lateral movement using WMI and SMB, and persistence via a custom loader named DUBLOADER that uses side-loading of libcurl.dll to execute encoded payloads.

indicators.context: An SQL server process related to the Veeam Backup instance executed a shell command
The script contains an embedded payload that is executed through reflective PE injection. POWERTRASH is an obfuscated loader written in PowerShell that has been attributed to FIN7
An additional file called "445.ps1" was dropped and executed on the compromised Veeam backup servers
A custom PowerShell script, "host_ip.ps1", was executed to resolve IP addresses to hostnames
A custom PowerShell script, "gup18.ps1", was executed to set up an active foothold in the compromised machine by creating a persistence mechanism
The PowerShell script was hosted on an external file-hosting service "temp[.]sh"
The PowerShell script drops 7 files, which are embedded in the script content, including gup.exe – Legitimate GUP.exe binary (part of the Notepad++ application)
libcurl.dll – .NET DLL file side-loaded by gup.exe
JZ4qWKZW – Encoded DICELOADER payload that’s loaded and executed by libcurl.dll
jkBDfXaL.bat – Batch file that executes gup.exe
0JNvHvAz.vbs – VBScript file that executes the batch file
TCP open port 9401 exposed to the internet. This port is used for communication with the Veeam Backup Service over SSL
The script performed remote injection into the 'PlugPlay' service, which made a network connection to a remote host on port 443

A custom PowerShell script was executed through lateral movement to gather operating system information on the target through the usage of WMI. The content of the script and the execution method is identical to activity associated with FIN7
The threat actor used a series of commands as well as custom scripts to gather host and network information from the compromised machines. Some of these commands included: netstat
The threat actor used a series of commands as well as custom scripts to gather host and network information from the compromised machines. Some of these commands included: tasklist
The threat actor used a series of commands as well as custom scripts to gather host and network information from the compromised machines. Some of these commands included: ipconfig
SQL commands were executed to steal information from the Veeam backup database

ttp_mappings.relevance: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in Veeam Backup & Replication exposed on the internet via TCP port 9401.
Multiple PowerShell scripts were executed including POWERTRASH, gup18.ps1, 445.ps1, host_ip.ps1.
The SQL server process copied Web.config to system.js, possibly to avoid detection.
Custom PowerShell script executed through WMI for discovery and lateral movement.
Custom PowerShell script sets up persistence via autorun registry entry and drops files in %APPDATA%.
The attack chain includes exploitation of a vulnerability to gain access and potentially escalate privileges.
Commands like netstat, tasklist, ipconfig were used to gather host information.
The host_ip.ps1 script resolves IP addresses to hostnames, which may be used for C2 communication.
The script sets an autorun registry entry to establish persistence.
While not directly mentioned, the exploitation of a known vulnerability suggests an initial access vector that could be related to phishing or other attack vectors.

logsource_suggestions.reasoning: Captures process execution including PowerShell scripts and sqlservr.exe which are key to the attack chain.
Detects file creation and modification including dropped files like gup.exe, libcurl.dll, and scripts.
Detects outbound connections to external IPs and ports, such as the connection to temp[.]sh or C2 servers.
Detects registry modifications for persistence mechanisms like autorun entries.
Captures PowerShell script execution including POWERTRASH and gup18.ps1 which are core to the attack.

rules_yaml:
title: Exploitation Attempt of CVE-2021-26084 Confluence OGNL Injection
id: 5e3d9b7c-4a2f-4b3e-8d1a-9e0f2c4d6e8f
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects exploitation attempts of the CVE-2021-26084 OGNL injection vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Server or Data Center.
    The attack targets the /pages/createpage-entervariables.action endpoint with a queryString parameter,
    which allows arbitrary code execution without authentication. This rule monitors web server logs for
    requests containing the vulnerable endpoint and attacker-controlled input.
references:
    - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-26084
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/doc/confluence-security-advisory-2021-08-25-1077906215.html
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains: 'createpage-entervariables.action'
        cs-uri-query|contains: 'queryString'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative access to Confluence using the createpage endpoint
level: high

title: Potential Remote Code Execution via OGNL Injection in Confluence
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-a1b2-c3d4e5f67890

    condition: selection
